🔴 The #1 Critical Bug to Fix First
Total Distance is 0.00 km on ALL screens. This is the core of the whole system.
Root cause: Either (a) GPS location points are not being saved to the backend during a trip,
OR (b) the distance calculation function is not running when the trip ends,
OR (c) the distance is calculated but not written back to the trips.total_distance_km column.
Fix this one bug first — everything else (claims amount, compliance %) depends on it.

PROMPT 1 — Distance Calculation Audit (Fix the 0.00 km bug)
I have a Node.js + Express + PostgreSQL backend for a GPS trip tracking app.
The app records location points during a trip (table: locations with columns: trip_id, latitude, longitude, recorded_at).
When the trip ends (POST /trips/:id/end), it should calculate total distance using the Haversine formula across all location points and write it to trips.total_distance_km.
Current problem: total_distance_km is always 0.00 after trip end.
Please audit the following and fix all issues:
1. Show me the correct SQL query to fetch all location points for a trip ordered by recorded_at.
2. Write a TypeScript haversine function that takes an array of {latitude, longitude} objects and returns total km (filtering out noise < 5m).
3. Show me how to call this function inside the trip end handler and UPDATE the trips table.
4. Write a one-time SQL migration to recalculate total_distance_km for all existing completed trips using their stored location points.

- Validate: employee has no currently active or paused trip (prevent duplicate active trips)
- Create trip record: status="active", start_time=NOW(), employee_id from JWT

- Return: { trip_id, status, total_distance_km, claim_id, claim_amount }

Audit my Socket.IO location ingestion pipeline for a GPS tracking app.
Setup: Node.js + Socket.IO v4 + PostgreSQL + Redis (Upstash).
Mobile app emits: socket.emit("location:update", payload) every 15 seconds.
Write the complete Socket.IO handler for the /tracking namespace that does ALL of the following:
1. Authentication middleware: validate JWT from socket handshake auth.token, attach user to socket.data
2. On connection: join employee to room "employee:{userId}", log connection
a. Validate payload with Zod schema: { trip_id, latitude, longitude, accuracy_m, speed_kmh, is_mock, recorded_at }

f. Broadcast to all manager rooms that have this employee assigned: emit "location:broadcast" with { employee_id, lat, lng, speed_kmh, trip_id }
4. On disconnect: log last seen, mark employee offline in Redis
Include the batch INSERT function for locations table (bulk insert for performance).
Include the Redis broadcast logic to find which manager rooms to broadcast to.
